pagetitle: "Campaign data demo: overview"
---

# Motivation

**Research campaign data management**

- Observations span instruments, teams and storage locations.
- A campaign release needs an identifiable dataset revision.
- Large files should be available without copying everything.
- This demo will evaluate DataLad as an alternative to IPFS.

**Current status:** documentation and publishing foundation only.

# Requirements

- Version campaign datasets and their component datasets.
- Retrieve selected files and verify their integrity.
- Record enough provenance to investigate and repeat processing.
- Discover observations by location and time.
- Expose management operations through a standard API.

# Why DataLad?

- Git history for dataset structure and small metadata.
- git-annex for large file content stored outside Git.
- Subdatasets record component revisions in a parent dataset.
- DataLad run records connect commands with inputs and outputs.

**To evaluate:** usability, recovery and scale with a realistic campaign.

::: {.notes}
References: https://docs.datalad.org/en/stable/ and
https://docs.datalad.org/en/stable/generated/man/datalad-run.html
:::

# Proposed architecture

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| DataLad + Git | Campaign structure, revisions and provenance |
| git-annex + S3 / MinIO | Large file references and external content storage |
| STAC | Metadata catalog and asset discovery |
| pygeoapi | Management operations and execution status |

**All integrations are planned.** The documentation includes the architecture diagram.

# Campaign datasets and subdatasets

```text
campaign/                 parent dataset
├── instruments/
│   ├── radar/            subdataset
│   └── radiometer/       subdataset
└── products/             subdataset
```

- Each subdataset has its own history.
- The parent records a specific revision of each component.
- Researchers retrieve only the content they need.

# S3 storage

- Evaluate a git-annex S3 remote with a MinIO endpoint.
- Keep large file content in object storage and Git history in a Git remote.
- Keep credentials outside datasets and published metadata.
- Verify remote copies and recovery before removing local content.

**Planned:** storage configuration and a retrieval demonstration.

::: {.notes}
Reference: https://git-annex.branchable.com/special_remotes/S3/
:::

# STAC discovery

- Start with a static catalog of standard Collections and Items.
- Describe spatial and temporal coverage.
- Link assets to retrievable data at the intended revision.
- Resolve authentication and asset URL lifetime before publication.

**Planned:** catalog generation. No custom metadata schema is defined.

::: {.notes}
Reference: https://stacspec.org/en/about/stac-spec/
:::

# pygeoapi operations

- Candidate processes: campaign registration, availability checks and catalog refresh.
- Keep management functions usable independently of the API.
- Use OGC API Processes for execution results and job status.
- Choose asynchronous execution only when workflows need it.

**Planned:** process plugins. Continuous monitoring remains a design question.

::: {.notes}
Reference: https://docs.pygeoapi.io/en/stable/publishing/ogcapi-processes.html
:::

# DataLad versus IPFS

| Aspect | DataLad + git-annex | IPFS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity and history | Git revisions and annex keys | CIDs, with history designed separately |
| Availability | Copies on configured remotes | Providers retaining or pinning content |
| Provenance | DataLad run records | Additional tooling or conventions |
| Discovery | Proposed STAC layer | Discovery layer also needed |

**No benchmark results yet.** Compare the same data and access pattern.

::: {.notes}
References: https://docs.datalad.org/en/stable/ and
https://docs.ipfs.tech/concepts/persistence/
:::

# Next steps

1. Create a small synthetic campaign with two subdatasets.
2. Demonstrate S3 content retrieval and recovery.
3. Record one reproducible transformation.
4. Generate and validate a standard STAC catalog.
5. Expose one management process and compare with IPFS.
